results.content:
The New York Fed’s Survey of Consumer Expectations for July, released on Aug. 7, shows short-term inflation expectations edged down by 0.1 percentage point while medium and longer-term held steady. Perceptions about the current financial situation improved from a year ago, with a larger share of households reporting a better financial situation compared to those reporting a worse one. The perceived likelihood of losing a job in the next 12 months increased, as did the perceived probability of [...] Inflation. Median one-year inflation expectations fell by 0.1 percentage point to 3.6%. Medium-term expectations were unchanged at 3.3%, as were longer-term expectations at 3.0%.

results.title: Conference Board: Consumer Confidence Ticks Down in August

results.content: Expectations for the future held up somewhat better. The Index of Consumer Expectations fell 5.8 points to 63.5, essentially matching the lowest level in the survey’s 15-year history, last reached in March 2022. However, unlike the current conditions measure, the expectations index is largely unchanged from a year ago.
results.title: Consumer sentiment tumbles as Virginians feel pressure from inflation, new poll finds

results.content:
Inflation expectations among euro-area consumers inched down in July, easing European Central Bank concern over price risks from the Iran war.

Consumer prices were seen rising 2.9% over the next year, down from 3% in June, a monthly survey by the ECB showed Friday. The three-year gauge, which is more important for setting monetary policy, fell to 2.7% from 2.8% the previous month.
results.title: ECB Says Consumers’ Inflation Expectations Edged Down in July - Bloomberg
